newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-RANGERS WIN PLAYOFF DEBUT, ORIOLES ROUT CLEVELAND.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-RANGERS WIN PLAYOFF DEBUT, ORIOLES ROUT CLEVELAND.

text.p: The Texas Rangers made their post-season debut a memorable one as Juan Gonzalez and Dean Palmer homered in a five-run fourth inning to lead the playoff novices to a 6-2 win over the New York Yankees.
John Burkett went the distance, outpitching Yankees ace David Cone to give the Rangers a 1-0 lead in the best-of-five American League divisional playoff series.

"Everybody's relaxed and excited because it's the first time here," said Gonzalez, who had 47 homers in the regular season. "This is great for us and the fans. They've been waiting a long time, 25 years."
In the other AL playoff opener the Baltimore Orioles used the long ball to rout the visiting Cleveland Indians 10-4.
Burkett, acquired from the National League Marlins in August, had never faced the Yankees. He scattered 10 hits, walked one, struck out seven and pitched out of jams in the first and sixth innings.
Cone, who was sidelined for four months following surgery to repair an aneurysm in his right shoulder, had only one really bad inning, but it cost him the game.
Cone had allowed just one bloop hit through three innings and held a 1-0 lead when Gonzalez came up with two men on and sent a liner into the left-field bleachers, giving Texas a 3-1 lead.

Will Clark then singled sharply to centre and Palmer hit a liner to almost the same spot as Gonzalez's homer, just beyond the reach of leaping left fielder Tim Raines, to silence the record crowd of 57,205 at Yankee Stadium.
"I looked great early, in the fourth inning I started to lose my command," Cone said. "I made some pretty bad pitches in the fourth inning.

"Obviously we've got to win tomorrow night. It's not good to lose the first game but we're not dead by any means," added Cone, who struck out eight, but allowed six runs and eight hits in six innings.

The Yanks got a run back in the bottom of the inning when Mariano Duncan singled home Tino Martinez. But New York left runners at first and third when Derek Jeter bounced into an inning-ending force play.
Texas added the final run in the sixth when Mark McLemore singled home Mickey Tettleton.

The Yankees squandered a golden opportunity in the sixth with Bernie Williams and Martinez on first and third with none out. But Burkett struck out Darryl Strawberry and Duncan and got Jeter to pop out with the bases loaded.
"John Burkett was in control the entire ballgame," said Texas manager Johnny Oates.
Earlier in Baltimore, the homer-happy Orioles slugged four round-tripper to clobber the Indians.

Bobby Bonilla belted a grand slam to cap a five-run sixth inning that broke the game open, B.J. Surhoff smashed a pair of solo shots and Brady Anderson added a signature lead-off homer to power Baltimore, which set a major league record this season with 257 home runs.
Game Two in the best-of five series is set for Wednesday in Baltimore.
The regular umpires worked all the playoff games, but the officiating was in doubt nearly until the opening pitch.
Substitute umpires stood ready to replace the regulars, who threatened to boycott over the handling of the suspension of Orioles second baseman Roberto Alomar.

Umpires were outraged that Alomar was not suspended immediately for spitting in the face of umpire John Hirschbeck during a dispute last Friday. The umpires agreed to work after a hearing on Alomar's conduct was moved up to this Thursday.

The Orioles led 5-3 when Bonilla came up with the bases loaded against Cleveland reliever Paul Shuey. Bonilla ripped a low fastball into the right-field seats to give the Orioles a game-breaking 9-3 bulge.
"It's really wonderful. It was very exciting," he said.
David Wells got the victory, allowing four runs and eight hits in 6 2/3 innings. Cleveland starter Charles Nagy was roughed up for seven runs and nine hits in 5 1/3 innings.

"Bobby had a tremendous hit, Brady got it going again. Wells did what he had to do for us," said Surhoff, who became the first Oriole to hit two homers in a playoff game since Eddie Murray in the 1983 World Series.
"We've got to win tomorrow," said Nagy. "Going down 0-2, it's tough to come back in a five-game series. Tomorrow is a must win, then we go home and win two of three."
